{{short description|British physicist (born 1957)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2022}}
'''Sir Duncan John Wingham''' (born 12 October 1957) is a British physicist who is professor of climate physics at [[University College London]], and was the first director of the [[Centre for Polar Observation & Modelling]]. He was chief executive (January 2012 - January 2018) and Executive Chair (January 2018 - June 2023) of the [[Natural Environment Research Council]] and principal scientist for the [[CryoSat Satellite Mission]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cpom.org/people/djw/ |title=CPOM Website |access-date=25 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070526030734/http://www.cpom.org/people/djw/ |archive-date=26 May 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the 1990s, Wingham was involved in a four-year satellite study of the Antarctic ice sheet. His conclusion then, and from later research, is that the Antarctic has contributed little to observed rising [[sea levels]] in the 20th century. However, he has also stated that "it is possible that the consequences of [[global warming]] on [[sea level rise]] have been underestimated... Other sources of rise must be underestimated. In particular it is possible that the effect of global warming on thermal expansion [on the oceans] is larger than we thought".<ref>[[The Independent]] 16 October 1998 – extracted from:[https://books.google.com/books?id=8zZNwpkv1X0C&dq=Professor+Wingham&pg=PT253 Sandra Amos and Richard Boohan; ''Aspects of Teaching Secondary Science''; Routledge] {{ISBN|0-415-26082-5}}</ref>

In a 2005 interview Wingham stated "[t]he Antarctic is to some extent insulated from global warming because to its north are zonal flows in the atmosphere and ocean, unimpeded by other landmasses... I am not denying global warming."<ref>Pelle Neroth Taylor; ''[http://www.theregister.co.uk/2005/02/24/ice_shelf_collapse/ Natural causes to blame, expert claims]''; [[The Register]]; 24 February 2005</ref>

Wingham was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2020 New Year Honours]] for services to climate science.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=62866|supp=y|page=N2|date=28 December 2019}}</ref>
